metric.name: runtime_majority_share
metric.loc_definition: Physical lines with at least one non-comment token; blank lines and comments excluded. Python docstrings count as code lines. Rust doc and block comments do not.
metric.runtime_scope: Production functions/modules synchronously used from request admission through decision, authorization/consume, process/tool dispatch, response enforcement and owned cleanup, for the product runtime roots: hook HTTP/CLI events, guard-run, direct command/runtime evaluation, package shims/protect/launch, MCP proxy/surface/tool calls and supported direct/frozen routes.
metric.global_exclusions: Tests, fixture constructors, benchmarks, generated catalogs/programs, vendored code, comments/blank lines, offline compiler/authoring-only code, frontend assets, and genuinely asynchronous control/persistence code off the request path.

python.import_policy: static ast closure over eager and lazy imports (TYPE_CHECKING blocks ignored, literal importlib.import_module followed); module granularity

exclusions.reason: Plugin-scanner product (offline scan, scoring, reporting); reached from the package __init__/CLI hub or AIBOM inventory but never invoked on a request-admission-to-enforcement route.

AIBOM inventory/export and trust-metadata reporting; control-plane reads for dashboards/cloud sync, not on the enforcement path. aibom_detection and the inventory_contract fingerprint/model modules stay in scope: adapter detect() and hashing run synchronously during launch.

Wake-driven/background Cloud Review sync, replay and outbox delivery; asynchronous persistence and network delivery outside the synchronous request path. runtime/exact_cloud_review.py, exact_cloud_review_apply.py and exact_cloud_review_diagnostics.py hold the exact-review executor, apply and status logic; they are called only from the excluded command queue, executor, transport, cloud-review settings, connect-time consent and native-workspace-review modules. In-scope code reads constants from them (store_native_workspace_review's revocation state key) and review_exact_capability_advertisement calls _verified_capability and _capability_digest from exact_cloud_review.py to build the queue-eligibility advertisement. That call is reached only through review_contracts.build_local_review_request_claim, whose callers are the background claim paths (cloud_review_event_projection, local_request_snapshots listing for sync, and exact_cloud_review_apply); it is asynchronous claim projection and is not invoked from hook admission, decision, consume or dispatch.
Guard Cloud command-queue worker and executors; remote job processing, not request-path enforcement.

Extension/contribution authoring, discovery, probing and custom-extension profile management (offline builder or dashboard control plane). Modules the hook evaluation calls synchronously (package_json_scripts, custom_extension_suggestion, mcp_server_contribution, extension_contribution) stay in scope; only continuity sync, catalog sync/handshake and builder/control surfaces are excluded.
Codex/MCP setup, host inventory and registry browsing; configuration management, not enforcement.

Guard self-update orchestration (release download, staging, desktop apply, repair); CLI/daemon lifecycle, not request path. onefile_open_paths.py is reached only from GuardDaemonServer._reclaim_onefile_extraction_dirs_once, the hourly (3600 s) _onefile_extraction_reclaim_loop thread, and the excluded repair engine.

Install/uninstall/doctor/connect/pairing/OAuth/desktop-bootstrap CLI flows and repair/inverse lifecycle. codex_hook_recovery.py/codex_hook_rollback.py are the hook-publication journal, called only from CodexHarnessAdapter._write_authenticated_hook_config_owned, prepare_* migration/backup functions, prepare_install, the shim and cursor prepare functions and the excluded repair/inverse modules. shell_profile_cleanup.py is reached only from shims.remove_guard_profile_blocks (uninstall). commands_remove_hooks, hook_removal_presence, daemon_stop and commands_repair back the uninstall/repair CLI commands and are imported only by the commands_support facade and the excluded parser/dispatchers.

Argparse construction, Rich rendering and onboarding/status presentation for CLI subcommands that are not runtime routes. cli/render.py stays in scope because hook responses are redacted and emitted through it; only the doctor/uninstall renderers are excluded. commands_support_service.py (service login/status/sync, daemon start/stop/status handlers) is imported only by the commands_support facade and the excluded admin, cloud and records dispatchers.

Managed-device health-lease reporting, lifecycle and removal authorization; cadence-driven machine reporting independent of harness activity. Managed-policy loading (mdm.policy, contracts, network, file locks, device-key and integrity helpers) stays in scope because config loading and the daemon invoke it synchronously during hook handling.
Approval-center/dashboard daemon APIs and daemon lifecycle plumbing (local CLI grants API, command-activity API, diagnostics, reapers); control plane served beside, not inside, the hook route.

Core-owned runtime transition coordination, qualification and capture; one-shot activation lifecycle rather than per-request enforcement. runtime_transition.py (RuntimeTransition, TransitionFile, TransitionError, assert_transition_mutation_allowed) is reached only from install, uninstall, prepare, migrate and repair functions: adapters/base.py (PreparedHarnessInstall.publish, prepare_install, _owned_adapter_mutation), the adapters' prepare_install/install/uninstall/_install_owned/_uninstall_owned/prepare_codex_* methods, cursor_hooks._prepare_cursor_hooks, codex_hook_manifest.prepare_authenticated_hook_*, codex_hook_integrity._ordinary_hook_writer, shims.prepare_guard_shim/install_guard_shim/remove_guard_shim/ensure_guard_shim_path_in_shell_profile, store_cloud_events.set_managed_install (called only by install/bootstrap/paseo install), and the excluded transition coordinator modules. No hook, run, protect or MCP route calls it.

hol-guard-secrets repository/staged/pre-commit scanner CLI; separate product entry point, not a Guard runtime route. secrets/__init__.py and secret_detection.py (SECRET_RULES, SecretFinding, SecretScanSummary) are imported only by the repository/staged scanners and the secrets CLI; cli.py reaches the package only through main() for the `secrets` subcommand.
Python string templates that emit TypeScript/JS/shell harness hook assets at install time; generated artifacts, not Python executed on the request path.

Cloud connect, OAuth refresh/DPoP, receipt, runtime-session, supply-chain-bundle and policy-bundle sync transport (runtime/runner.py). Every public entry point (sync_receipts, sync_runtime_session, sync_supply_chain_bundle, sync_local_guard_cloud_proof, prepare_guard_cloud_connect_authorization, repair_guard_cloud_connect_storage, the cloud-review and command-queue workers and the daemon's cloud policy-bundle and managed-controls delivery handlers that import its urlopen/auth/bundle helpers) runs from `guard connect`/`guard sync`, the cloud-review sync worker or the command-queue loop, never inside hook admission, decision or enforcement. The Rust runtime has no HTTP client, so the network, token refresh and retry loop stay in Python by design; the policy computation inside it (payload shaping, scrubbing, cursor/ack arithmetic, verdict digests, bundle verification) already runs in the resident through runner_native_sync/runner_native_authority. The only request-adjacent caller is the Hermes launch credential lookup (guard_run_launch._resolve_hermes_guard_access_token), which reads the cached token and, when it is absent or near expiry, runs the same OAuth refresh HTTP request as `guard sync` before the harness starts. That refresh is network transport the Rust runtime cannot perform; the lookup is best-effort, runs once at the execution boundary after the authority verdict, and never decides admission. The run-side lookup wrapper stays in scope.

Explicit and periodic Guard repair: `guard repair` (cli/commands_repair), POST /v1/repair and the removal endpoint (daemon/repair_api via _handle_repair_api) and the 600 s repair self-check thread (daemon/repair_self_check started by _start_repair_self_check). None runs inside hook admission, decision or enforcement. resident_state_prune.py and daemon/runtime_repair.py are reached only from repair_engine (repair_native_runtime, repair_daemon) and the daemon package's lazy export used by the repair CLI handler.

reviewed_runtime.reason: Reviewed: module is a decision, parser/scanner, transport, process-dispatch or containment component invoked by a runtime route.

Reviewed: cli support/router/render: hook payload, interaction, runtime resolution and policy, permission store, connect and workspace helpers, the command router and lifecycle gate (run/protect), and cli/render.py. Reached synchronously from cli/commands_support_hook_payload and commands_hook_native_pipeline on every native hook request, and from commands_router.run_guard_command for run/protect. render.py is kept whole because its native-hook emitters share the module with presentation code; function-level scoping is a follow-up.

Reviewed: adapters: harness registry targets (codex, grok, zcode, mcp_servers, cursor native approval, hermes file inspection, capability_report, attestation and path helpers). Loaded through the dynamic adapter registry and reached from approvals.py, cursor_hooks, hook workers and launch_command for run/protect. Install/diagnostics methods share the classes with the launch and approval paths, so the files stay whole in scope.

Reviewed: codex hook inventory, identity, sources, trust, registration, owner commands/preflight, foreign-group and health modules: codex_hook_trust_stale is called from codex_native_hook_state, which gates launch_command/preview_launch_commands for codex, and it imports registration, owner_commands and foreign_groups; runtime_trust is used by frozen_codex_runtime.trusted_hook_launch; inventory/identity/sources are used by the same adapter. codex_hook_owner_preflight and codex_hook_health are tiny status/install-only modules left in scope under the in-doubt rule.

Reviewed: daemon client and peer modules: client/response_bounds are the hook-to-daemon transport; runtime_peer/live_identity authenticate the live daemon; recovery_lifecycle is invoked from daemon/manager on hook-failure recovery; policy_authority_client is called from local_supply_chain; claude_permission_request is called from hook_worker.

Reviewed: runtime support modules used by supply-chain evaluation, contained execution, local-CLI/MCP grant decisions and secret-file-request services: js_semver, npm_policy_range, lockfile/manifest evaluation, package_json_scripts, source_paths/skill_paths, local_node_runner_*, typescript_snapshot_inputs, contained_test_hook/wrapper, oci isolation, extension and mcp_server contribution, embedded_script_evidence, executable_flag_contract, local_cli_compound, mcp_connection_identity, mcp_server_grants. Each is imported by an in-scope decision, parser or containment module on the hook/run path.

Reviewed: guard MCP server (mcp/*): the `guard mcp` stdio server answers tool calls (policy, registry, adapters) from agents, so it is an MCP-surface request route; classified in scope under the in-doubt rule. Entry: cli/commands_dispatch_local -> mcp/server.

Reviewed: shared policy, inventory, store and consumer modules: consumer/service (runtime runner), capabilities, product_model (argv harness dispatch in the top-level CLI on every invocation), local_cli_*/local_mcp_grant_decision trust decisions (native_mcp_tool_policy), business_policy_document_import (policy snapshot publisher and recovery), store_* mixins on the policy/MCP/extension paths, skill_document_evidence, trust_metadata_boundary, inventory_item_description, text.py, runtime_transition_hook_probe (daemon/server), codex_binding_capture_join, cloud_exceptions (store_cloud_events) and policy_bundle_decisions (local_supply_chain policy-bundle handling).

tests.note: repository-level Python tests, not part of the package

function_exclusions.reason: Rich and plain-text renderers, panel and table builders, and the renderer dispatch tables that format Guard command results for a human terminal. They compute no verdicts and read no stores; they only lay out an already-built payload.
function_exclusions.evidence: The retained reference closure of every symbol other modules import from render.py (_redact_payload, _render_redacted_json_payload, emit_guard_payload) contains none of the excluded symbols except through emit_guard_payload, whose as_json=True branch (the only branch the hook protocol uses: commands_support_hook_payload.py writes JSON through _redact_payload and _render_redacted_json_payload directly) never reads them. The excluded symbols are reached only from emit_guard_payload's as_json=False branch through the _RENDERERS and _PLAIN_TEXT_RENDERERS tables. The report validates this reference closure on every run.

function_exclusions.reason: HarnessAdapter default install, prepare_install and uninstall implementations used when an adapter does not override them.
function_exclusions.evidence: The default prepare_install, install and uninstall are invoked only from the excluded install, uninstall and repair command dispatchers. No retained runtime code reads these attributes. The report validates that no retained symbol or in-scope module references the excluded names.

The report validates that no retained symbol or in-scope module references the excluded names.
